rules.title: Never commit directly to main
rules.rule: Never push to `main`; create a topic branch from the current `main` and open a pull request targeting `main`.
rules.rationale: Direct pushes bypass the review gate and can publish unreviewed or broken work.

rules.title: Say Mission, never feature
rules.rule: The canonical product term is Mission (plural: Missions). The words `feature` and `features` are prohibited in canonical, operator, and user-facing language when they refer to the domain object.
rules.rationale: Terminology drift makes the domain model ambiguous.

rules.title: No blanket noqa
rules.rule: A lint suppression must name the specific rule code it suppresses and carry a short rationale; a bare `# noqa` that suppresses everything is not allowed.
rules.rationale: A blanket suppression hides new findings as well as the one intended.

rules.title: One trailing newline, no trailing whitespace
rules.rule: Every source file ends with exactly one trailing newline and contains no line with trailing whitespace.
rules.rationale: Avoids noisy diffs and toolchain churn.

rules.title: Conventional Commits
rules.rule: Commit subjects follow `type(scope): subject`, where `type` is one of the repository's allowed types (for example `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`).
rules.rationale: A machine-readable history lets tooling group and validate changes.

rules.title: Format and lint before push
rules.rule: Run `ruff format --check .` and `ruff check .` before pushing; both must pass.
rules.rationale: Formatting is a separate gate from linting.

rules.title: Prefer a durable fix over a shim
rules.rule: When a structural cause produces a defect, fix the structure rather than hiding the symptom behind a shim. If a shim is genuinely unavoidable, say why in the change.

rules.title: Read the charter before planning
rules.rule: Read `.kittify/charter/charter.md` before planning or changing code; it is the binding governance document and carries rules not repeated elsewhere.
rules.rationale: The charter carries rules not repeated elsewhere.
